name: Clonmacnoise

attributes.attribute: buried place of seven high kings incl. Ruaidri Ua Conchobair

text: Clonmacnoise is a monastery on the eastern bank of the Shannon in Co. Offaly, thirteen miles south of Athlone. St Ciarán founded it on 25 January 545. It grew into the leading early monastic site of Ireland, one that in church standing only Armagh could rival. In early Christian art and learning it had no equal. Its scribes produced Lebor na hUidre, the early Irish codex Book of the Dun Cow. Raiders, native and foreign, attacked the site countless times. Monks held on until an English force stormed it in 1552. The monastery then lay abandoned. Surviving remains include five high crosses, parts of nine churches, and two round towers. More than five hundred early gravestones survive, many bearing inscriptions. Seven high kings (ard ríthe) found burial here. They include Ruaidri Ua Conchobair, the final ruler of that line, who died in 1198.

okr.objective: Clonmacnoise is St Ciarán's great Shannon monastery, peerless in early Christian art and letters.
key_results: St Ciarán founded the house on 25 January 545 on the Shannon shore in Co. Offaly.
Only Armagh matched its church standing, and it led the making of early Christian art and books.
Its scribes produced the Book of the Dun Cow, and the site fell only after an English sack in 1552.
Nine churches, five high crosses, two round towers, and over five hundred gravestones remain from seven buried high kings.
okr.evidence: MacKillop, Dictionary of Celtic Mythology, s.v. Clonmacnoise
